parts.article:
A closer examination of a study on verbal and non-verbal messages
 
A study of non-verbal communication carried out in 1967 continues to be widely quoted today. David Lapakko looks at limitations in the original study.
 
Description of the Study
(A) The findings of a study on verbal and non-verbal messages in communication by Albert Mehrabian and his colleagues at UCLA in 1967 have been quoted so frequently that they are now often regarded as a self-evident truth.
 
(B) In the first experiment, subjects were asked to listen to a recording of a female saying the word “maybe” in three tones of voice to convey liking, neutrality, and disliking. The subjects were then shown photos of female faces expressing the same three emotions and were asked to guess the emotions in the recorded voice and the photos. It was found that the photos received more accurate responses than the voices. In the second experiment, subjects listened to nine recorded words spoken in different tones of voice. Three words had positive meanings (e.g. honey), three were neutral (e.g. oh), and three were negative (e.g. terrible). Again, the subjects had to guess the speaker’s emotions. It was found that tone of voice carried more meaning than the individual words. From these experiments the researchers concluded that 7% of our feeling towards a speaker is based on the actual words they use, 38% on their tone of voice, and 55% on their body language (e.g. facial expression).
 
Methodological Issues
(C) However, a closer look at the study reveals several limitations. The first is that the entire study involved only 62 subjects. Of these, 25 were used to select the word for the first experiment, while the key issue – comparing verbal and non-verbal communication – was determined by only the 37 remaining subjects. All were female undergraduates who participated as part of their introductory psychology course, and their ages and academic qualifications seem remarkably uniform. Thus, the findings may simply be a product of the nature of the sample.
 
(D) Critics have also pointed out that the 7–38–55 formula is flawed since it was pieced together from two different experiments, neither of which involved all three channels (verbal, vocal, and facial). In addition, in the first experiment the single word “maybe” was used throughout so it was impossible for the effects of changes in verbal input to be assessed. The researchers intentionally used a “neutral” word so naturally the subjects found little meaning there. Clearly, such a methodology lacks validity. In the real world, people communicate in a particular context and speak in phrases and full-blown sentences, making extensive use of the multi-faceted vehicle of language.
 
(E) My concern is that interpretations of this study have gained such prominence in our pedagogical literature. This 7–38–55 formula appears in many basic texts, used for training in public speaking, interpersonal communication, and organizational communication.
 
Lessons to consider
(F) Clearly, one appealing aspect of the Mehrabian study is its numerical precision. Communication is a complex phenomenon, but it seems less so when we can rely on these three magical numbers. In contrast to the ambiguities of language, numbers seem to possess exactness. And the popular appeal of the study has given the 7–38–55 formula enormous credibility. There is a certain mystique about non-verbal communication, and the continued references to this research sustain it, encouraging people to believe in the overwhelming importance of the non-verbal message compared with the verbal one. Yet we know that even one ill-chosen word to a colleague or friend can make or break a communicative effort. Words do matter. Bradley (1991), one of the few textbook writers to criticize the Mehrabian study, makes the same point when he observes, “If we could communicate 93% of information and attitudes with vocal and facial cues, it would be wasteful to spend time learning a language.”
 
(G) Mehrabian himself believes his research should not be interpreted to devalue the role of language in communication, saying: “Please remember that all my findings… dealt with communications of feelings and attitudes… it is absurd to imply or suggest that the verbal portion of all communication constitutes only 7% of the message… anytime we communicate abstract relationships (e.g., x = y – the square of z) clearly 100% of the entire communication is verbal.” (Mehrabian, 1995)
 
(H) To be fair, many textbook writers attempt to be faithful to the context of Mehrabian’s research. For example, Stewart and D’Angelo (1988) write: “Mehrabian argues that when we’re uncertain about what someone’s feeling, or about how much we like him or her, we rely… only 7% on the words that are spoken.” Others try to play down the specific percentages, saying that an understanding of the general importance of non-verbal cues is more important. Nonetheless, other textbook authors simply use the numbers without placing any limits on their meaning.
 
Conclusion
(I) Since this relatively small study was first published it has achieved an influence far beyond its intended scope. We need to put it into its proper perspective and learn some important lessons from it regarding social science research, communication pedagogy, and the forces which have created widespread misunderstanding about communication.

analyses.content: 你可能想选 "characteristics"（特征），但文中并没有详细描述信息的特征，而是重点在于它们对听众判断情感时的不同分量（即影响）。

Description of the Study: The findings of a study on verbal and non-verbal messages in communication by Albert Mehrabian and his colleagues at UCLA in 1967 have been quoted so frequently that they are now often regarded as a self-evident truth.
文中提到该研究主要针对“语言和非语言信息”在沟通中的表现，结合后文提到的各项百分比（7%, 38%, 55%），可以看出研究是在比较这两种信息产生的“影响”或“效果”。
文中明确提到，受试者在听录音和看照片后，需要去猜测其中的“emotions”（情绪），这与选项中的 "feelings" 是同义替换。
不要看到 "gender differences" 就选，虽然受试者都是女性，但实验任务是识别情感，而不是区分性别。
Description of the Study: The subjects were then shown photos of female faces expressing the same three emotions and were asked to guess the emotions in the recorded voice and the photos.
第一个实验中，受试者听了声音，然后看了“表达三种情绪的女性面部照片”，这直接对应“面部表情”。
这里是对比声音和视觉线索，照片展示的就是表情，而非“printed words”（那是第二个实验的内容）。
Description of the Study: The subjects were then shown photos of female faces expressing the same three emotions and were asked to guess the emotions in the recorded voice and the photos.
你可能想选 "printed words"，但实验的核心变量是单词所代表的“含义”（积极/消极），而不仅仅是印刷形式。
第二个实验中使用了三类词：积极含义、中性含义和消极含义，研究发现语调比“individual words”（单词本身）更重要，这里比较的就是语调与“词义”。

Description of the Study: Three words had positive meanings (e.g. honey), three were neutral (e.g. oh), and three were negative (e.g. terrible). ... It was found that tone of voice carried more meaning than the individual words.

questions.question: One limitation of the study was that there were too few subjects involved.

analyses.content: 作者在指出的第一个局限性中，明确批评整个研究只涉及了62名受试者，这直接对应题目说的“受试者太少”。
Methodological Issues: The first is that the entire study involved only 62 subjects.

questions.question: The fact that the subjects in the study came from a similar background was an advantage.

analyses.content: 作者指出受试者全是心理学入门课程的女大学生，背景高度一致，导致结果可能只是该特定样本的产物，这意味着背景相似是“劣势”而非题目说的“优势”。
不要觉得实验控制变量（背景一致）就是好事，这里作者是在批评样本缺乏代表性。
Methodological Issues: All were female undergraduates... and their ages and academic qualifications seem remarkably uniform. Thus, the findings may simply be a product of the nature of the sample.

questions.question: The two experiments should have been carried out in a different order.

analyses.content: 文中分别描述了两个实验的内容和缺陷，但从未提及它们的“顺序”是否错误，或者是否应该调换顺序。
Description of the Study: In the first experiment... In the second experiment...  (文中仅按顺序叙述，无对顺序优劣的评价)。

questions.question: The researchers’ choice of a neutral word was helpful in the context of the study.

analyses.content: 你可能认为控制变量是“helpful”的，但在作者看来，这在现实沟通语境中是不自然的，因此是负面评价。
Methodological Issues: The researchers intentionally used a "neutral" word so naturally the subjects found little meaning there. Clearly, such a methodology lacks validity.
作者认为研究人员故意使用“中性词”导致受试者自然无法从中找到意义，只能依赖语调，这种方法论是“缺乏有效性”（lacks validity）的，即这种选择是不合理的。

questions.question: The study would have been more valid if it had included a range of languages.

analyses.content: 作者提到现实世界中人们使用“短语和完整句子”以及“多层面的语言工具”，但并没有具体讨论如果包含“多种不同的语言”（如法语、中文等）是否会提高有效性。

Methodological Issues: In the real world, people communicate in a particular context and speak in phrases and full-blown sentences, making extensive use of the multi-faceted vehicle of language.  (只提到了语言的形式，未提多语种)。

analyses.content: Bradley 的逻辑是反证法：如果我们真的可以用非语言手段传达93%的信息，那花时间学语言就是浪费；既然我们花力气学语言，说明语言（Words）必然很重要。
A选项错在 Bradley 并不是在谈论学习效率，而是通过“学语言很费时”这个事实来反驳“语言不重要”的观点。

analyses.content: 这一段以 "To be fair" 开头，列举了三种教材作者：有的忠实于原意，有的试图淡化百分比，有的则不加限制地滥用数字，这展示了对该研究的不同解读方式。
A选项错在作者不是在“证明”研究的优点，而是在陈述不同人如何“使用/解读”这个研究。

Lessons to consider: To be fair, many textbook writers attempt to be faithful... Others try to play down... Nonetheless, other textbook authors simply use the numbers without placing any limits on their meaning.
